Date of Order : 05.12.2025  3 C.C. No. 3898 / 2022  JUDGMENT The present complaint is filed under section 200 of code of criminal procedure against the accused seeking to punish him for the offence punishable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act ( in short referred as "N.I. Act").
02.
The facts which leads to file the present complaint are narrated as under.
It is contended that, the Complainant knows the accused through her father and they are family friends.
The accused working as Lecturer and the Complainant is an anchor.

In the month of May 2018 on various occasions the accused has demanded to the Complainant for advancing hand loan to resolve his family problems and as per her fathers instructions, she had paid in all a sum of Rs.9 lakhs till the end of October 2018 by way of cheque through the account her father.

The accused has assured to repay the said amount within 2 years 9 months and has issued 2 post dated cheques bearing No. 025900 dated 28.07.2021 for Rs.4,50,000/- and another cheque bearing No. 044488 dated 28.07.2021 for Rs.4,50,000/- .

Both the cheques were drawn on Fedaral Bank, Tiptur Branch,
Tumkur District.
It is further contended that, on the assurance of the accused, the Complainant has presented the aforesaid both the cheques with his banker for encashment on 28.07.2021.
But they have returned unpaid due to "Funds insufficient" in the account of the drawer as per bank return memo dated 30.07.2021.
Thereafter pn 13.08.2021 he got issued demand notice to the accused through his advocate by RPAD.
RPAD issued to re residential address of the accused is served on 17.08.2021 and RPAD sent to his office address returned.
The accused neither has paid the cheque amount not has given any reply.
Therefore it is prayed to punish the accused under section 138 of NI Act and to impose fine the double cheque amount and to award compensation.
03. On presentation of the complaint, this court has verified the averments of the complaint and also annexed documents.
Having made out prima facie case cognizance has been taken for the offense punishable u/s 138 of NI Act.

As per the verdict of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Indian Bank Association V/s. Union of India and others sworn statement of the Complainant has been recorded as PW1 and in all got marked 11 documents at Ex.P1 to P11.

04. In response to the court summons, the accused put his appearance before the court through his counsels and filed bail application under section 436 of Cr.P.C., along with necessary applications,
since the alleged offense is bailable in nature, accused has been enlarged on bail.
The plea has been recorded and read over to the accused and he pleaded not guilty and wish to put forth his defense.
As per section 145 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, sworn statement of the Complainant has been treated as affidavit evidence and the accused has been permitted to cross-examine of PW1.

05. Heard arguments advanced by both the learned counsels.
The Learned defense counsel has relied following citations.

The following points that arise for my consideration are as under;
POINTS 1.

Does the complainant proves beyond reasonable doubts that, the accused has issued 2 post dated cheques No. 025900 dated 28.07.2021 for Rs.4,50,000/- and another cheque bearing No. 044488 dated 28.07.2021 for Rs.4,50,000/- .

Both the cheques were drawn on Fedaral Bank, Tiptur Branch, Tumkur District towards the discharge of his lawful liability of the complainant and when the said cheques were presented for encashment, they were returned unpaid due to shara as "Funds insufficient" as per banker's memo and in-spite of issuance of demand notice, the accused have failed to pay the cheque amount,
thereby has committed the offence punishable under section 138 of NI Act?
2. What Order or sentence ?
07. My findings to the above points is as follows;
1. Point No.1: In the Negative 2.
Point No.2:

It is the specific case of the complainant that, from May 2018 to October 2018 on various dates she has advanced a sum of Rs. 9 lakhs to the accused through account of her father and accused has issued disputed cheques to repay the said debt.
When the Complainant has presented both the cheques with his banker, they have returned unpaid due to "Funds insufficient" in the account of the drawer.
Therefore in spite of issuance of demand notice and service of the same the accused failed to pay the cheque amount.

Accordingly, it is sought to convict the accused under section 138 of Sindhu C vs Bhanuprakash M C on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60673389/
3 NI Act.
09.

Ex.P1 and P2 are the disputed cheques, Ex.P3 and 4 are the bank return memos, Ex.P5 is the demand notice, Ex.P6 is the returned closed RPAD cover,

Ex.P7 is the postal acknowledgment, Ex.P8 is the RC Book Card, Ex.P9 and P10 are the Reliance General Insurance Policy copies, Ex.P11 is tEx.P8 is the RC Book Card,

To disprove the case of the Complainant and also to rebut the Legal presumptions which could be drawn in favour of complainant the accused by name Bhanuprakash M C himself has entered into the witness box and adduced his oral evidence as DW1 and got marked in all 2 documents.
Ex.D1 and D2 are the policy copies of star life insurance.
Both the learned counsels have cross examined their rival witnesses comprehensively.

10. Before to appreciate oral and documentary evidence produced on records, it is imperative on this court to find out whether the Complainant has proved the necessary ingredients of section 138 of NI Act before filing the present complaint.

11. Looking upon the disputed cheque, bank return memos and demand notice at Ex.P1 to P5 it can be seen that, the disputed cheques have been presented with bank within its valid period and demand notice was issued within 30 days from the date of receiving the bank return memos.
As per postal acknowledgment at Ex.P7 the addressee has personally received the RPAD cover by putting his signature on the acknowledgment.
Whereas the return RPAD cover bears the note of the postal authority stating that, it was kept for 7 days and due to door lock it was returned to sender.
By considering these postal reports it appears that, the accused has personally received the demand notice at Ex.P7.
But as per Ex.P6 it was not received by the accused.
During the entire cross examination of PW1 nor in the oral evidence of accused no dispute has been raised about non service of the demand notice.

On the other hand in his cross examination at Page No.2 the accused himself admitted that, after receiving the demand notice, he met the Complainant and enquired about sending notice, for which the Complainant replied that I will set right and don't worry.
Which means the accused has personally received the demand notice.
The present complaint has filed before this court on 04.10.2021.
Thus, now it can be concluded that the present complaint has been filed before this court only after the fulfillment of the requirements of section 138 of NI Act.
12. Section 118 & 139 of NI Act are two important provisions and they provides for raising mandatory presumptions in favour of the complainant until the contrary is proved by the accused.

Even in the catena of decisions i.e., in the case of Rangappa Vs. Mohan reported in 2010(11) SCC Sindhu C vs Bhanuprakash M C on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60673389/
4 441, in the case of Bir Singh Vs. Mukesh Kumar reported in 2019(4) SCC 197, in the case of APS Forex Services (P) Ltd., Vs.Shakthi International Fashion Linkers reported in 2020(12) SCC 724, in the case of Rajeshbai Muljibhai Patel Vs. State of Gujarat, reported in 2020(3) SCC 794, in the case of Triyambak S. Hegde Vs. Sripad reported in Live Law 2021 SC 492 , a precedent is laid down that,
" Once the issuance of cheque and the signature thereon is admitted by the accused, the court is required to raise presumption in favour of the the complainant stating that, the accused has issued the cheque for some consideration towards discharge of his legal debt or liability of the complainant and that the complainant is the due holder of the said cheque.

Now, it is well established law that, the presumption mandated by section 139 of NI Act, thus indeed includes the existence of legally enforceable debt or liability and it is open for the accused to raise a probable defense wherein the existence of legally enforceable debt or liability can be contested and he shall prove before the court on preponderance of probabilities
, only thereupon a statutory presumption raised in favour of the complainant stands rebutted.

13. The Learned defense counsel has relied the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2014(2) SCC 236 in the case of John K Abraham Vs. Simon C Abraham and another with due respect to the ratio of the said case and considering the fact of the case on hand, I am of the firm opinion that this ratio in the case of John K Abraham Vs. Simon C Abraham and another is not applicable to the case on hand.

sentences.text: From the above relied judgment complied with the provisions of section 118 and 139 of NI Act, now it is well settled law that, once the issuance of cheque and signature thereon is admitted, the Legal presumptions under section 118 and 139 of NI Act shall works in favour of complainant, it is burden on the accused to rebut the Legal presumptions.
Once succeeds in rebutting Legal presumptions, onus heavily shifts on the Complainant to prove his case beyond all reasonable doubts.
In the instance case admittedly, the accused has failed to put forth his defense in the beginning by giving reply notice.
However, there is no bar for the accused to put forth his defense during the trial of the case.
During the cross examination of PW1 the signature at Ex.P1(a) is not at all disputed.
During the cross examination of DW1 in para 3 of page No.1 the accused has admitted his signatures on the cheques at Ex.P1(a) and P2(a).
Therefore the Legal presumptions shall works in favour of complainant.

During cross of PW1 on page No.2 of dated 29.04.2025 it is suggested to PW1 that, the accused has borrowed Rs.50,000/- from the father of Complainant in the year 2019 and at that time her father has taken two signed cheque leafs and the documents shown in Ex.P11.

In order to prove this defense the accused Bhanuprakash M C has stepped into the witness box and led his oral evidence as DW1 stating that, since 15 years he has been running Zenith Academy, wherein he takes tuition classes for the students of High School and PUC.
He testified that, the Complainant is stranger to him and no money transaction has taken place between him and herself
He further testified that the father of Complainant by name Chandraprakash Gupta was close to him and the said Gupta was working as Manager in Merchants Bank at Tipatur.

He further said that, he had opened account of Zenith Academy in the bank in which father of Complainant was working as Manager, he spokes that, the father of Complainant was also insurance agent and has insured a car policy.
He used to tall similar amount from said Chandrashekar Gupta.
The said Chandrashekar Gupta undertakes to get insurance police of his car and his health.
He reveals that, due to spread of covid -19 , he has closed Zenith Academy and during the said period he was under gone financial crises, therefore he has availed Rs.50,000/-

He deposed that, while taking hand loan,
Chandrashekar Gupta has taken his signed two blank cheques and on the reopening to his Zenith Academy in the month of August 2020 he had repaid entire amount of Rs.50,000/- to the father of Complainant and at that time it was under taken to return the cheque but later did not returned.

However, when he has received demand notice from the Complainant advocate in the year 2021, he has went to the house of the Complainant and came to know that, Chandrashekar Gupta is no more who died in Covid and he said that, he has not taken any hand loan from the Complainant and not issued disputed cheque sto the Complainant , the cheque given to her father is misused by the Complainant and has filed false case.
The Learned defense counsel has cross examined DW1 comprehensively.

14. On careful evaluation of the oral evidence of Complainant and the accused as well as the documents produced by the Complainant at Ex.P8 to P11 and at Ex.D1 to D2 it is admitted fact that,
the deceased father of the Complainant by name Chandrashekar was known to the accused.

In para No.4 of the complaint it is specifally pleaded stating that, the Complainant had paid to the accused hand loan as requested by him on various occasions by way of cheque i.e. through her fathers accounts cheque and cash totaling amount a sum of Rs. 9 lakhs till the end of October 2018.

To substantiate and to prove this fact, the Complainant neither has produced her bank account statement nor the bank account statement of her father and she has admitted this fact in her cross examination.
This pleading under para No.4 of complaint is like omni bus.
To prove this fact the self serving testimony of PW1 is insufficient.

When the Complainant himself says that, on various dates or occasions she has advanced Rs.9 lakhs in all within a period of 6 months, she has to give details with regard to on which day or in which money she had advanced how much amount by way of cash or by way of cheque.
This pleadings is totally absent.
More over it is not stated how much amount was paid in cash and how much amount was padi by way of cheque.
This fact has been admitted by PW1 In her cross examination.

In her cross examination dated 29.04.2025 at page No.2 when she was suggested that the accused was used to take small hand loan from her father oftenly, she has denied the said suggestion but she herself given explanation in her later cross examination that some amount was paid from the account of her father.

When PW1 herself is admitting or stating that some amount was paid from account of her father, that fact very much corroborate the oral evidence of accused with regard to his defense contending that, he had borrowed Rs.50,000/- from her father.
When the accused is very much denying his acquaintance with the Complainant, then she must give explanation as to how she came in custody of the documents Ex.P8 to P11.
These are the RC book and General insurance policy copies.
This RC book of a vehicle standing in the name of accused.
The blank form No.29 along with sale receipt, copy of insurance and authorization letter bears signatures of the accused.
Either in the complaint or in the affidavit evidence of Complainant no reasons have been shown as how or under what circumstances these documents have came to the custody of the Complainant .
On the other hand, the accused himself stated in his oral evidence that Chandrashekar Gupta was also the insurance agent.
This evidence of accused is neither disputed nor denied during the cross of DW1.
On the other hand, in para No.4 of cross examination the accused was suggested that, his insurance policy was submitted to Chandrashekar Gupta for renewal of his policy.

In his further cross examination of para No.5 a suggestion has been made from the Complainant side stating that, he had handed over his documents at Ex.P8 to P11 as a security for the repayment of disputed debt.

In respect of this suggestion there is no pleadings in the complaint Sindhu C vs Bhanuprakash M C on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60673389/
6 so also no evidence in the chief of PW1.

On the other hand, the accused has produced Star health Insurance Policy which are marked at Ex. D1 and D2 wherein the father name of Complainant Mr.
Chandrashekar Gupta is shown as intermediary.
Which means the father of Complainant also working as insurance agent and through him only the accused has got these two health policies.
That apart, during her cross examination PW1 has stated that, in respect of this disputed debt, the accused has executed one  , but she has not produced the said   before the court.
Even the Complainant neither pleaded in the complaint no has spoken in her affidavit evidence what is her income either monthly or annually.
Running of Zenith Academy in the Tiptur of Tumkur District is not disputed by the Complainant .

The Complainant herself has admitted that,
her father has died in the Tiptur only, and her father as well as mother were residing in Tiptur only that fact very much corroborate the testimony of the DW1 with regard to his acquaintance with deceased Chandrashekar Gupta and also his taking health insurance policy from her father.
Therefore by considering and evaluating the oral and documentary evidence placed on record.
I am of the considered opinion that, the accused has put forth probable defense and proved the same by producing cogent and acceptable evidence.
I have carefully gone through the judgments relied by the Learned defense counsel, with due respect, they are aptly applicable to the case on hand.
Thereby the accused has successfully rebutted the Legal presumptions.
On the other hand the Complainant has failed to prove her case beyond all reasonable doubts.
Accordingly, I answered point No.1 in the Negative.

POINT NO.2:
15.

In view of the above findings, this court proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
Acting under Section 255(1) of code of criminal procedure, the accused is acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
The bail bond of accused and surety stands canceled subject to appeal period.
